The ROI is roughly 10 km wide and 10 km tall. The drone flies at 90 m AGL.
- Radar: 5 km range, needs line of sight, cost 4.
- EO: 6 km range, needs line of sight, cost 3.
- RF: 8 km range, no line of sight needed, cost 2.

The SW quadrant has the highest weight (3), followed by NW (2), and NE/SE (1).
Site 17 is in the SW (x=-1.27, y=-6.55) with a very low horizon (max 13.9 deg, mostly < 2 deg). It is the best site for the SW quadrant.
Site 6 is in the SW (x=-6.11, y=-3.52) with a low horizon (max 18.7 deg, mostly < 10 deg). It is the second best site for the SW quadrant.
Site 11 is in the NW (x=-3.74, y=2.66) with a moderate horizon (max 18.5 deg). It is the best site for the NW quadrant.
Site 15 is in the NE (x=3.10, y=2.44) with a very low horizon (max 4.4 deg). It is the best site for the NE quadrant.
Site 13 is in the SE (x=1.66, y=-3.13) with a low horizon (max 13.3 deg). It is the best site for the SE quadrant.

To maximize detection probability, we should place sensors with the longest range (RF) at the best sites in the highest-weighted quadrants.
- Site 17 (SW, weight 3): RF (cost 2)
- Site 6 (SW, weight 3): RF (cost 2)
- Site 11 (NW, weight 2): RF (cost 2)
- Site 15 (NE, weight 1): RF (cost 2)
- Site 13 (SE, weight 1): RF (cost 2)

Total cost: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10. We have 3 cost units left.
We can add another RF sensor to a site in the SW quadrant to increase coverage there.
Site 7 is in the SW (x=-5.74, y=-5.49) with a low horizon (max 10.1 deg). It is a good site for the SW quadrant.
- Site 7 (SW, weight 3): RF (cost 2)

Total cost: 10 + 2 = 12. We have 1 cost unit left.
We cannot afford another RF sensor (cost 2). We can afford an EO sensor (cost 3) or a radar (cost 4), but we only have 1 cost unit left. So we cannot add any more sensors.

Wait, let's re-evaluate the budget.
Budget: 13 cost units.
Placements:
- Site 17: RF (cost 2)
- Site 6: RF (cost 2)
- Site 11: RF (cost 2)
- Site 15: RF (cost 2)
- Site 13: RF (cost 2)
- Site 7: RF (cost 2)
Total cost: 12.

We have 1 cost unit left. We cannot afford any more sensors.
Is there a better combination?
Maybe we should use EO or radar instead of RF?
RF has the longest range (8 km) and does not need line of sight. It is the most efficient sensor in terms of range per cost unit (8/2 = 4 km/cost unit).
EO has a range of 6 km and needs line of sight. It is less efficient (6/3 = 2 km/cost unit).
Radar has a range of 5 km and needs line of sight. It is the least efficient (5/4 = 1.25 km/cost unit).

So, RF is the best choice.
We have placed 6 RF sensors at the best sites in each quadrant, with extra coverage in the SW quadrant (the highest-weighted quadrant).
The total cost is 12, which is within the budget of 13.

The drone is a fiber-optic FPV with no radio emissions and no Remote ID broadcast, so Remote ID receivers and RF detectors have zero detection range against it and are useless here. Only radar and EO thermal cameras can detect it, and both require line of sight.

Radar costs 8 and reaches 6.2 km; EO costs 3 and reaches 2.4 km. With a budget of 18, I can afford two radars (16) plus one EO (3) = 19, which exceeds budget. So options: two radars (16) + no EO, or one radar (8) + three EO (9) = 17, or one radar + two EO = 14, etc.

Radar has much longer range (6.2 km vs 2.4 km), so it covers far more of the ROI from a single site. EO is cheap but short-range. Since the ROI spans roughly 8 km across, a single radar at a high, open site can cover a large fraction. Two radars at well-chosen sites can cover most of the ROI.

Site 4 is at (5.14, -2.57), elevation 959 m (+213 m above median), with very low horizon angles toward E (1°), SE (4.2°), S (1.1°), SW (2.7°), W (0.6°) — excellent open view to the south and west. It can see most of the ROI from the east side.

Site 3 is at (1.36, 5.11), elevation 879 m (+133 m), with low horizon toward NE (5.2°), E (-2.7°), SE (-3.5°), S (-2.5°) — good view to the south and east. It can cover the northern part of the ROI.

Site 9 is at (0.51, 5.51), elevation 935 m (+189 m), with low horizon toward E (3°), SE (-2.4°), S (-3.5°), SW (-1.7°) — also good southern view.

Site 1 is at (3.70, -4.40), elevation 870 m (+123 m), with low horizon toward E (-0.6°), SE (-2.1°), S (-3.3°) — good southern view from the southeast.

To maximize coverage, place radars at sites with the best line of sight and highest elevation to cover the most ROI. Site 4 (east, high, open to west/south) and site 3 (north, high, open to south) are strong candidates. Their ranges (6.2 km) should cover most of the ROI from these vantage points.

Cost: 2 radars = 16, leaving 2 budget. I can add one EO (cost 3) — no, 16+3=19 > 18. So I can only afford 2 radars (16) and have 2 left, which is not enough for EO (3). Alternatively, 1 radar (8) + 3 EO (9) = 17. But radar covers much more area per unit cost.

Given the ROI is large and the drone is small, radar's long range is critical. Two radars at sites 4 and 3 should provide overlapping coverage over most of the ROI. The remaining 2 budget cannot buy an EO, so I'll stick with 2 radars.
